text:
### Observed differences

- Before, each of the five activities A31, A32, A37, A38 and A39 ran exactly once in every case; in the later window each runs in about 55 in 100 cases (110 of 200), and the five always run together as one group, in no single fixed internal order in either window. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL030, REL039]
- A22 shows the mirror image: it ran in every case before and runs in about 45 in 100 cases (91 of 200) in the later window. [OCC001]
- Before, all of A20's outgoing transitions led into the group (about 17–24 in 100 to each member); in the later window A20 leads to A23 in about 995 in 1,000 observed transitions, and the close succession of A20 to a group activity within five steps, present in all 200 earlier cases, appears in only one later case (each later lag profile rests on a single observation). [DIR001, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]
- Before, A21 was always followed by A22; in the later window A21 is followed by A22 in about 45 in 100 of its observed transitions and by the group activities in about 55 in 100. [DIR002]
- The group's order relative to A21 and A23 reversed: before, the group always preceded both; in the later window A21 and A23 precede the group in nearly every case where both occur, with the old group-first order remaining in about 1 in 200 cases. [REL008, REL012, REL020, REL024]
- A22 and the group, which previously always ran in the same case (group first, A22 later), now almost never do: co-occurrence in about 1 in 200 cases, group alone in about 55 in 100, A22 alone in about 45 in 100. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019]
- The hand-over after the group changed: before, each group activity passed to A23 in roughly 17–26 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window that flow goes to A26 instead (about 14–26 in 100). A22 still precedes A26 when it runs, and the group still precedes A26. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL014, REL025]
- Event positions moved consistently with this: the group's mean position shifted from about 0.40 to about 0.57–0.59 of the trace, A23's from about 0.48 to 0.38 and A21's from about 0.62 to 0.53 (event positions, not clock time). [POS002, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A19 fell from a mean of about 0.94 hours (median about 0.93) to about 0.45 hours (median about 0.45), on 56 observations in each window. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The control-flow family flagged 72 items where about 0.7 would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, so the flagged control-flow behaviour as a whole cannot be a sampling artefact; the single time item, by contrast, is of the size an unchanged process occasionally produces (1 item against about 0.02 expected). [OCC001–OCC006, DIR001–DIR007, POS001–POS010, REL001–REL039, LAG001–LAG010, TWAIT001]

The evidence supports the possibility that the five-activity group A31, A32, A37, A38, A39 was rerouted and made conditional, while A20, A23, A21 and A26 remained in every case. Before, every case ran A20, then the group in an unfixed order, then A23, later A21, A22 and A26; in the later window, A20 leads almost directly to A23, and after A21 the case either runs the group (about 55 in 100 cases) or A22 (about 45 in 100) — the two became mutually exclusive alternatives — with both branches leading to A26. The support is direct and consistent: successor changes at A20, A21 and every group member, reversal of the group's order relative to A21 and A23, near-zero co-occurrence of A22 with the group, and matching participation and position shifts. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, OCC001, OCC002, REL008, REL015, REL020, POS006]

Limitations: the lag profiles of the rerouted pairs rest on a single later observation each, so the exact spacing of the moved group is not established, and the evidence cannot show whether the choice between the group and A22 is a within-case decision or reflects two different case populations in the later window. [LAG001–LAG010]

Other differences: the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A19 roughly halved (mean about 0.94 to about 0.45 hours, 56 observations per window); as a lone time item it is of the kind an unchanged process occasionally produces, so a timing change on this pair is not independently established, and any connection to the rerouting cannot be determined from the evidence. [TWAIT001]
